fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Off-Grid Living as a Training Ground", "body": "Benjamin Balderson describes a farm life lived completely off grid, with spring water caught and gravity fed to his house, his own chickens and milk cows, and almost no bills. He argues that people spend countless hours at jobs so they can pay others to do what they could do themselves, and he says he fixed his own truck for sixty dollars in parts. Chance Garton adds that the age of information makes ignorance a choice, and that the things we own end up owning us."}, {"title": "Cold Extraction and the Three Levels of Oil", "body": "Ben says every carbon-based life form breaks into three levels, salt, oil and carbon, and that the oil itself divides into three. Using cannabis as his example, he walks through terpenes, CBD and THC as layers separated by volatility. His own lab work runs at negative forty degrees on flash-frozen plant picked before dawn, ideally near the full moon, because he holds that heat damages oil for good. He frames oil as the feminine side and salt as the masculine, a polarity he returns to all episode."}, {"title": "Cymatics, Salt, and the Memory of Water", "body": "Ben plans to build a library of cymatic patterns in the spirit of Masaru Emoto, so that shapes can be read as messages. He argues that water itself does not hold memory, salt does, which is why Emoto's distilled water, stripped of salts, could be written on. His proposed experiment sends a message in dried salt to Chance, who would dissolve it, flash freeze it and read the pattern. Chance wonders whether symbols carry an inherent meaning that cymatics could finally reveal, and Ben pushes further, claiming sound and thought precede light."}, {"title": "Crystals, Missing Elements, and the Great Work", "body": "Ben rejects the familiar four elements as truncated, arguing that fire, water and air are only the feminine half, and that a crystalline, structured side is always left out. He maps seven levels of elements, joins the most chaotic with the most dense in an Ouroboros, and says demonizing the salt side is what disempowers people. Chance shares his selenite experiments with light. For Ben, the great work means descending to the deepest salt as well as ascending, then bringing both back to the middle."}, {"title": "A Cosmic Battery and the Cycle of Seasons", "body": "Ben presents a world model in which the sun is a gold cathode and the moon a silver anode, with planets as metal plates in one vast galvanic cell, so that silver becomes gold. He then maps spring, summer, fall and winter onto a cycle of masculine and feminine, reading spring as the reforging of the sword and the return of the king. Prompted by Chance's question about an emasculated society, Ben says we sit at the end of a cycle, in a high feminine winter."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Heathen wizard (and practical modern Alchemist) Benjamin Balderson joins InnerVerse to chat about salt and oil, sun and moon, and other aspects of the life-fractal that we can explore to help us achieve our own great work, transmute our toxins into treasures, and bring balance to our biorhythms.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Pasteurization and the Choice to Buy Local", "body": "Ben agrees that pasteurization is horrible, saying it kills the life in milk and leaves the gut to do the work, yet he says there is not much evil in it. His own cow's milk sours within days, while commercial milk waits in tanks, factories and stores, so Ben argues consumers cannot demand both long shelf life and raw freshness. Chance draws the line at evil when someone is arrested for selling milk, and floats bringing back the milkman. Ben predicts things must worsen until people grow their own food."}, {"title": "Spagyrics and the Lego Bricks of the Body", "body": "Asked about cell salts, Ben explains spagyrics as breaking a plant into oil, salt and earth, and says the body has three levels of salts with four salts apiece. He compares body structure to Lego bricks, claiming that replacing a worn brick with a Duplo weakens the whole castle over time. He says fat, an excellent mercury in his terms, makes salts absorbable, and he calls silica quartz. Chance asks which easily missed symptoms might point to a cell salt need, and Ben answers from his own alchemical framework."}, {"title": "Salts of Salvation, Sodium, and the Body's Electricity", "body": "Ben introduces Dr. Carey's salts of salvation, twelve cell salts set out along the zodiac, each pairing set against its opposite as contraction faces release. He criticizes common table salt as processed and describes sodium as the water bearer. Salts, he argues, set the body's electroconductivity, just as they do in a plant, and without them the brain turns sluggish. He recalls army runs where his clothes were caked with salt. These are Ben's convictions, offered in a cosmology that links organs to salt."}, {"title": "Mercury Figures and Odin's Great Work", "body": "Ben sorts gods into mercury, sulfur and salt figures, and says the mercury figure stands in the middle with access to both sides, as Odin, Hermes and Zeus do. Robin Hood becomes his perfect mercury story, a hero from below and a thief from above. Chance asks whether Odin or Hermes is an actual being or part of ourselves. Ben answers with the Odin mind, the well and Yggdrasil, a path through nine worlds, and a claim that ancestral wisdom is written in the densest salts."}, {"title": "Distilled Water, Ormus, and Myths as Alchemy", "body": "Chance asks about distilled water, and Ben replies that water is a mercury, so distilled water will grab whatever salts it meets, which he thinks suits only a salt overload. On Ormus, he separates electrolysis of mineral salts from the classical monoatomic gold. He reads the story of Vulcan, Venus and Mars as a recipe for an alloy made with white fire. Chance says stories carry symbols forward through lost ages, and Ben links salt overload to the biblical pillar of salt."}]

fields.Plus Quotes JSON: [{"text": "We can blame the system, but there's not really that much evil in it.", "author": "Benjamin Balderson", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/9076d077-da2c-4992-abc8-c4cc7575dc14/BENJAMIN-BALDERSON.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "You could never run out of ways to wonder about the unity in life as a single force flowing.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "When we get to the point where we literally are starving, then we are gonna go plant our own damn food because we have no choice.", "author": "Benjamin Balderson", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/9076d077-da2c-4992-abc8-c4cc7575dc14/BENJAMIN-BALDERSON.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Most people don't realize silica is quartz.
